description:
Procrastination is a strategy! A strategy to protect you from painful stimulus. So we feel the stress about a particular task, and procrastination is the strategy of ‘looking in the opposite direction’. 

Which is HIGHLY effective for avoiding the painful stimulus! The issue is that it doesn’t REMOVE the source of stress. That’s still there in the background, often becoming a bigger problem out of sight. But we still feel it, and it gets heavier and heavier.

SO, there’s one small thing you can do, to gradually chip away at your procrastination, and one big thing, that can transform it dramatically. 

1. The small thing; instead of trying to force yourself to do the thing you don’t want to do, investigate why you don’t want to do it. Investigate the resistance, the tension, the stress, and see if you can remove the source of THAT before trying to do the task. 

Remove a couple of things if you have to! But don’t bother with the task until you’ve done so. You’ll learn over time the kinds of obstacles that tend to crop up for you, and you’ll come up with your own strategies for removing them. It massively takes the sting out of the tasks we hate!

2. The big thing; do whatever you can to find 2-3 free weeks, preferably more, in which you can do NOTHING. I mean nothing productive at all. It might be the most productive thing you do in your life. 

But there’s one rule—you can ONLY do shit you enjoy IN THE MOMENT. If you binge 10 episodes of a show and then you start to get bored, you are no longer allowed to binge the show. If you start scrolling and 10 minutes you realise you’re not enjoying it, stop. Find something else to do, that you WILL enjoy. 

For as long as you can manage, ONLY do activities for as long as you enjoy them, then stop. Try it. If you’re a chronic procrastinator, it’ll change your life. 

And if you want to know how it works, or help with procrastination, perfectionism or purpose in general, get in touch through the coaching inquiry link in my bio. I’d love to give you a hand!
